en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Earth.
1. The Question on the Factors of the Earth “Venerable Nāgasena, as for what you say—that ‘five factors of the earth should be adopted’—which are those five factors that should be adopted?

“Just as, Great King, the earth remains exactly the same whether one scatters upon it desirable things such as camphor, aloe-wood, tagara, sandalwood, and saffron, or whether one scatters upon it undesirable things such as bile, phlegm, pus, blood, flesh, fat, saliva, snot, tears, urine, and excrement.”

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a yogāvacara, must remain exactly the same in all circumstances—whether toward the desirable and the undesirable, gain and loss, fame and disrepute, blame and praise, or pleasure and pain.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the earth that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the earth is free from adornment and decoration, yet it is suffused with its own fragrance.
In the same way, Great King, the yogin, the practitioner of yoga, should be free from ornamentation and perfumed by the fragrance of his own virtue.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the earth to be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the earth is continuous, without cracks or fissures, without hollows, thick, dense, and vast.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must possess virtue that is continuous, unbroken, flawless, unblemished, firm, dense, and vast.
This, Great King, is the third quality to be taken from the earth.

Furthermore, Great King, although the earth supports villages, market towns, cities, provinces, trees, mountains, rivers, ponds, lotus pools, wild animals, birds, men, and throngs of women, it does not become weary.
In the same way, Great King, a yogi who is a practitioner of yoga must not grow weary in his teachings of the Dhamma,
whether he is exhorting, instructing, informing, demonstrating, inciting, inspiring, or gladdening others.
This, great king, is the fourth quality of the earth that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, the earth is free from attraction and aversion;
even so, great king, the practitioner of yoga should dwell with a mind like the earth, free from attraction and aversion.
This, great king, is the fifth quality of the earth that should be adopted.
And this was said, great king, by the female lay follower Cūḷasubhaddā while praising her own ascetics:
“Even if one were to cut off an arm with an axe...”
With their minds provoked to anger toward her,
they would be delighted if she were to anoint even a single arm with perfume.
In that [other] there is no aversion,
and in this one passion is not found;
their minds are even like the earth.
“Such are the ascetics for me.
This is the first question on the constituent parts of the earth.
